title: Ramadan 2026: distribution in progress
label: Distribution in progress
description: Funds collected during Ramadan 2026 are now being distributed to people in need.
note: Status confirmed by Dost in September 2026. Distribution is ongoing; this update is not a final distribution report.
paragraphs: Dost collected donations during Ramadan 2026. Distribution is now in progress, with support being delivered to people in need.
This entry records the current stage of the 2026 campaign. A final account of the distribution is not yet available.
The latest completed distribution report in this archive covers 2025. It provides a record of how contributions from that year were used.

title: Medical care, school costs, and daily expenses
label: Distribution report
description: Support for seven families, including medical care, education, food, and daily essentials.
paragraphs: In 2025, the community raised $5,226. The report describes support for seven families in Afghanistan, with needs ranging from medical treatment and ongoing medication to education, food, and basic household expenses.

Approximately $600 in event ingredient costs and $130 in platform fees were paid from donations, leaving approximately $4,496 for family support. The organizers covered the venue, supplies, most ingredients, and money-transfer costs themselves.

The report does not provide exact allocations per family because support included ongoing treatment and medication. The figures here preserve that distinction rather than implying a complete family-by-family accounting.
note: This summary covers the 2025 distribution, although the source was published in February 2026. Amounts marked ≈ are approximate.

title: Support from friends and family
label: Yearly update
description: A private campaign brought together direct contributions from friends and family to support people in need.
paragraphs: In 2024, Dost organized a private fundraising campaign within its circle of friends and family. Supporters contributed directly, and the funds were distributed to people in need.
The campaign was organized internally, without a public fundraising appeal. Because contributions came directly from friends and family, Dost did not publish a public annual report at the time.
This update has been added to the archive to document that year’s work and explain how the campaign was supported.
note: Retrospective update, added in September 2026 based on the account provided by Dost. No fundraising amount or recipient count is stated in this record.

title: Project Food Drive: the 2023 Ramadan appeal
label: Project brief
description: An online appeal for food packages in Shahristan, with a published shopping list, delivery plan and commitment to cover distribution costs separately.
note: This page summarizes the 2023 campaign plan. The household target, food quantities and budget are planned figures. A final distribution update has not yet been supplied. Photographs on the campaign page are explicitly labeled as 2022 distributions, so they are not presented as 2023 results.
paragraphs: Project Food Drive’s 2023 online appeal sought contributions to buy staple foods for families in Shahristan, Daikundi. The initial target was 100 households, with an ambition to reach 150 if enough funding became available.

The published plan listed rice, flour, cooking oil and pasta. It described a package intended to help a family of four with food for about a month, at a planned cost of $107. Any additional contributions after the food distribution were intended for medication.

The organizer planned to transfer funds to trusted contacts in Afghanistan, who would buy supplies in Kabul and transport them to the village. The project page says labor, transport and transaction fees would be covered personally by the organizer.

sections.heading: How the project was organized
items: Fundraising took place online ahead of Eid.
Local contacts were to identify households with limited access to food or agricultural income.
Food was to be purchased in Kabul, transported to the village and distributed on a set date.
The campaign committed to sharing distribution photographs and updates.

title: Food assistance for 110 families in Daikundi
label: Distribution report
description: An April 2022 field update documents food packages for 110 families in Daikundi, Afghanistan.
note: Prepared from the dated Facebook record supplied by Dost. The English summary also draws on the accompanying Dari field report. The $6,000 is the reported amount sent; the post does not provide a complete expense reconciliation.
paragraphs: Ahead of Ramadan in 2022, Sara Daqiq collected contributions from friends and family and sent $6,000 to Afghanistan. Her Facebook update, dated April 1, records that the funds had been sent for distribution.

The field report shared by Zia Arman on the same date describes food assistance for 110 families in Daikundi. It lists flour, rice and cooking oil as the contents of the household packages. The photographs document people gathered with supplies at the distribution site.
The post describes support for households facing severe financial hardship. Contributions collected abroad were turned into essential food supplies and distributed locally.

sections.heading: What was provided
items: Cooking oil; the field post notes that the oil was not shown in the photographs

title: Food and basic necessities for 80 families
label: Distribution report
description: A May 2021 follow-up records completed assistance for 80 families in Daikundi, following the Ramadan appeal.
sourceLabel: Read the earlier May 9 fundraising plan
paragraphs: On May 28, 2021, Sara Daqiq reported that donations had helped provide basic necessities to 80 families. The update was accompanied by photographs of households gathered with food packages.
The field post shared by Zia Arman on the same date identifies the distribution area as Miramor district in Daikundi province. It describes packages containing flour, rice and cooking oil.

An earlier appeal, published on May 9, had proposed support for 60 families. The later Facebook update records the completed distribution to 80 families. This report uses the follow-up for the household count and keeps the earlier plan as background.
note: The completed household count comes from the May 28 Facebook update supplied by Dost. The earlier budget was a plan and is not presented as a final account of expenditure.

sections.heading: From appeal to distribution
items: May 9: the fundraising appeal set out a plan for 60 families.
May 28: the organizer reported that 80 families received basic necessities, supported by a field update and photographs.

title: Food packages in Shahristan, cash support in Kabul
label: Distribution report
description: Care packages in Shahristan and cash assistance in Kabul during the COVID-19 lockdown.
paragraphs: The report describes sending $5,000 to a trusted shopkeeper in Shahristan district for care packages. The planned support was adjusted to approximately $114 per household so that more families could be included.
A further $1,805.09 was distributed as cash assistance in Kabul. The report explains that photographs from Kabul could not be obtained during the COVID-19 lockdown.

The care-package account describes 44 households and estimates at least 308 people supported, based on seven people per household. That person count is an estimate, not an individually verified total.
note: The two reported distribution amounts total $6,805.09. The estimated people count is not used as a cumulative impact claim.

title: Eid food packages and cash assistance
label: Distribution report
description: Food packages and cash assistance, with allocations described household by household.
paragraphs: The organizer reported receiving $931.59 from GoFundMe after platform fees, plus a $100 family contribution, for $1,031.59 available before the reported $8 transfer fee.
Support combined food packages and cash according to household needs. When two intended recipients could not be reached, the report says families on a waiting list received support instead.
The original report lists individual allocations. This summary does not infer a final household count or a reconciled distribution total from the incomplete replacement-family details.
note: Funds received are distinct from the amount ultimately distributed. See the original report for the listed allocations.

title: Food and cash support for eight families
label: Distribution report
description: Food packages and cash assistance for eight families, documented in a follow-up published in 2019.
paragraphs: The report looks back on a 2018 fundraiser and describes food packages for six families, followed by cash assistance for two additional families in a remote area.
Its closing summary reports $1,300 distributed among eight families. Food packages included staples such as rice, flour, oil, and macaroni, with deliveries coordinated by relatives in Afghanistan.
This is the earliest distribution documented by the public reports currently linked here. It does not establish the organization’s legal incorporation date.
note: The work took place in 2018; the report was published in January 2019.
